D015-D005_h001.question:
I’ve been feeling down for over a year now—just constantly empty, like nothing matters. I used to enjoy organizing old manuscripts, finding little connections across centuries, but now I can’t even focus long enough to finish a single file. I keep forgetting where I put things, and it’s not just absentmindedness—it’s like my head’s always foggy. Some days, I think, “Maybe I’d be better off dead.” I don’t have a plan, but the thought is always there.

But that’s not the worst of it. For the past few months—long after the sadness started—I’ve been noticing things others don’t. I’ll feel something crawling on my skin, like bugs under my shirt, but when I check, there’s nothing. And people… I swear they’re talking about me. Even random comments on the bus or lines in books—somehow I just *know* they’re meant for me. Like the world’s sending me hidden messages. 

The strange part? These feelings—the itching, the being watched—they don’t just come when I’m sad. They’re there even on days when I feel okay. In fact, sometimes they’re worse when I’m not depressed at all.
